name: Ploy
summary: AI marketing platform that rebuilds your website from its URL and keeps working on it: AI-built pages, SEO and AI-search fixes, visitor identification, outreach and ad agents in one workspace, with a free tier.
best_for: marketing teams and startups that want an AI-built marketing site plus SEO, visitor identification and outreach agents in one platform, and are willing to move their site onto it
skip_if: you want a predictable fixed monthly price, only need a simple brochure site, or want to keep your site on your current builder and host
honest_knock: Pricing is credit-based and Ploy does not say how many credits a page, an edit or a Ploybook run costs, so the monthly bill is hard to predict in advance. The step from Starter at $50 to Pro at $300 is steep, and the HubSpot, Attio and ad integrations sit on Pro. A custom domain is not available on Free. Salesforce, SSO and SOC 2 are Enterprise only.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · Starter billed monthly with 4,000 credits a month and 1 custom domain
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-03 on ploy.ai/pricing) Ploy charges by plan and by credits. Credits are spent while Ploy is actively building or editing your site; the pricing page says a workspace that is just live and serving traffic uses next to nothing. Image generation, code generation, planning, visitor enrichment and Ploybooks all draw from the same credit balance. The Free tier costs $0, needs no card and includes 2,000 credits (the plan card says 500 credits a day, up to 2,000). Starter costs $50 a month with 4,000 credits a month, 1 custom domain family and 50 enriched visitors a month. Pro costs $300 a month with 24,000 credits, 5 custom domain families, 1,000 enriched visitors a month and the HubSpot, Attio and ad integrations. Annual billing costs 20% less: Starter $480 a year ($40 a month) and Pro $2,880 a year ($240 a month). Enterprise is custom priced and adds Salesforce, SSO, SOC 2, enterprise terms and done-for-you setup. Monthly plans can be changed at any time. Ploy does not publish how many credits a typical page or edit uses, so the real monthly cost depends on how much you build.

messages.subject: SEO & AEO audit: Waiting for your answer
Your website just got a new hire.

measured.tested_by: Our team; actor, account and scope are documented in the review.
method: Our AI assistant worked in its own tab of our browser, with the public site info.cern.ch as the source; the notes record what each screen showed and the screenshots have names and e-mail addresses masked

claims.claim: proposes a rebuild that only goes ahead once you approve it
claims.observed: After the site was entered Ploy asked three design questions and then built the design system, two images and three pages and published them on a production and a staging address on a Ploy subdomain, without a separate plan, price or page list to approve. The only approval was the answers to the three choice questions. The real site was not touched.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Ploy on the Free plan of an account we created, with the public site info.cern.ch as the source. About 6 minutes after the site was entered the first rebuilt page was visible (3 pages, a design system and two generated images) and about 2 minutes later Ploy published it on its own subdomain, after three design questions and without a separate step to approve the rebuild. One page with its design system cost about 226 of the 700 daily credits, and an audit chat that Ploy started by itself cost another 194. The pricing page gives the free plan 500 credits a day, the app 700. The Stripe checkout of Starter (EUR 454.53, billed annually) was seen and left with no card. Account and start: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab. The screen asked Verify your email (Check your inbox for a verification link); the verification mail from Ploy came in and the link was opened in that tab. No code or password was typed and no phone number was asked. The interface was already in English and the cookie banner was declined. The plan was Free. The dossier name is Ploy and the review is on MSS (mss/ploy-review.html). The source site for the test was info.cern.ch, a neutral public test site that is not ours. Core action, read a site and rebuild it: at 08:55 the site was entered (placeholder yourcompany.com) and Ploy said it would take a look at the website. The next screen, What do you want help with?, offered Site migration (marked Recommendation, with the line that Ploy can research and write pages today but cannot publish to a site it does not host, so you get drafts), Organic traffic (already on), Conversion rate optimization, Improve brand positioning, Ad campaigns and Find more qualified leads; only Organic traffic stayed on. What's the vision for your site?: Enhance my current design. Ploy then started two chats by itself, Getting Started and SEO & AEO audit, which spend credits in the background. Drive Ploy from Slack was set to Do this later and Google Analytics and Google Search Console were not connected. In the chat Getting Started Ploy summed up the site and asked three design questions (What should set the feeling at first sight?, What should the main images show?, What should carry over from today's page?); each got the first recommended answer. At 08:56 the first proposal came (Building your design system), at about 08:57 the design system was ready, and at 09:01:33 the first built page was visible: a new homepage http://info.cern.ch - home of the first website with the button Browse the first website, two generated images (an early-90s workstation and an accelerator tunnel), and the pages /who-invented-the-world-wide-web and /404, 3 pages in all. Ploy said I made your new homepage. It's publishing now; once it's live I'll share the links., and at 09:03 Publish finished on a production and a staging address on a Ploy subdomain. Time: about 6 minutes from entering the site to the first built page and about 8 minutes to published, with 11 clicks and 3 answers. Approval: there was no separate plan or quote of what a rebuild would cost and no list of pages to approve; the agent built the pages straight after the three choice questions and published them to the Ploy subdomain without asking. The real site info.cern.ch was not touched and no own domain was connected. Credits: Settings, Usage showed AI credits 89 / 700 (Resets Nov 20) and Lifetime credits 89 / 2,000 straight after the onboarding, then 395 / 700 and 417 / 700 after the homepage (Today 421). By chat: Getting Started 226 (design system, two images, homepage and one more page), SEO & AEO audit 194 (started by itself in the onboarding) and other activity 1. Building one page with its design system cost about 226 credits, about a third of the daily 700. Contact credits 0 / 25. Plans: In the app (Settings, Billing): Free, 700 AI credits a day, 700 credits / day (2,000 max), without custom domains or enriched traffic data. Starter $50, now $40 per month, billed annually (Save $120 per year), 4,000 credits / month, 1 custom domain, Google Ads, Meta Ads and LinkedIn Ads, 25 contact lookup credits, 50 visitor enrichment credits and CRM integrations, with A/B testing marked coming soon. Pro $300, now $240 per month, billed annually (Save $720 per year), 24,000 credits / month, 5 custom domains, 150 contact lookup credits and 1,000 visitor enrichment credits. Extra AI credits can be bought, and 100 contact credits cost $25. On the public pricing page ploy.ai/pricing: Free $0, No credit card required, 500 credits / day (2,000 max); Starter $50/mo, 4,000 credits / month, 1 custom domain; Pro $300/mo, 24,000 credits / month, 5 custom domains, CRM integrations (HubSpot, Attio); Enterprise Custom. Billed annually, Starter is $480 a year ($40 a month) and Pro $2,880 a year ($240 a month). The free allowance differs: the pricing page says 500 credits a day, the app says 700 credits a day, both with a 2,000 maximum. Checkout: Billing, Starter, Upgrade opened Stripe Checkout at once for a Starter subscription, billed annually, EUR 454.53, with fields for card number, expiry and security code, Apple Pay and Link. Nothing was filled in and the page was left at once. The Stripe page was in Dutch, so no image of it was kept. A card was not asked at sign-up, onboarding, building or publishing to the Ploy subdomain, only at the upgrade. Cancelling: on the Free plan there is nothing to cancel and Billing shows only Upgrade; cancelling or changing a paid plan was not seen. Settings, Personal has a profile and no delete button that we saw; Security has password, passkey and Log out. Workspace General has a Danger Zone with Delete Workspace, which was not clicked. Not tested: the HubSpot and Attio links (Pro), connecting an own domain (Starter), Slack, Google Analytics and Search Console, publishing to an own domain, the full result of the SEO & AEO audit, A/B testing (coming soon), entering a card and cancelling a paid plan. Clean up: the account and the workspace with the info.cern.ch test project stay, and so do the two published Ploy subdomain pages, which are public and hold a redesign of info.cern.ch. The own tab was closed and our other tab was not touched. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Ploy starts two chats by itself in the onboarding and they spend credits in the background: the SEO & AEO audit used 194 credits before we asked for anything. There was no plan or price of the rebuild to approve; after three design questions the agent built the pages and published them on a public Ploy subdomain without asking. The free allowance is 700 credits a day in the app and 500 on the pricing page. The Stripe checkout followed the browser language rather than the English interface.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: The HubSpot and Attio links of Pro.
Connecting an own domain and publishing to it.
Slack, Google Analytics and Google Search Console.
The full result of the SEO & AEO audit.
A/B testing, which is marked coming soon.
A paid plan, a card, tax and the final total; only the Stripe checkout was seen and left.
Cancelling or changing a paid plan; the Free plan has nothing to cancel.
Deleting the workspace; the Danger Zone was not clicked.
Export of a file into a kit, and reimport.

Session and source-reading date: 19 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 08:54 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Ploy on the Free plan of an account we created, with the public site info.cern.ch as the source. About 6 minutes after the site was entered the first rebuilt page was visible (3 pages, a design system and two generated images) and about 2 minutes later Ploy published it on its own subdomain, after three design questions and without a separate step to approve the rebuild. One page with its design system cost about 226 of the 700 daily credits, and an audit chat that Ploy started by itself cost another 194. The pricing page gives the free plan 500 credits a day, the app 700. The Stripe checkout of Starter (EUR 454.53, billed annually) was seen and left with no card. Account and start: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab. The screen asked Verify your email (Check your inbox for a verification link); the verification mail from Ploy came in and the link was opened in that tab. No code or password was typed and no phone number was asked. The interface was already in English and the cookie banner was declined. The plan was Free. The dossier name is Ploy and the review is on MSS (mss/ploy-review.html). The source site for the test was info.cern.ch, a neutral public test site that is not ours. Core action, read a site and rebuild it: at 08:55 the site was entered (placeholder yourcompany.com) and Ploy said it would take a look at the website. The next screen, What do you want help with?, offered Site migration (marked Recommendation, with the line that Ploy can research and write pages today but cannot publish to a site it does not host, so you get drafts), Organic traffic (already on), Conversion rate optimization, Improve brand positioning, Ad campaigns and Find more qualified leads; only Organic traffic stayed on. What's the vision for your site?: Enhance my current design. Ploy then started two chats by itself, Getting Started and SEO & AEO audit, which spend credits in the background. Drive Ploy from Slack was set to Do this later and Google Analytics and Google Search Console were not connected. In the chat Getting Started Ploy summed up the site and asked three design questions (What should set the feeling at first sight?, What should the main images show?, What should carry over from today's page?); each got the first recommended answer. At 08:56 the first proposal came (Building your design system), at about 08:57 the design system was ready, and at 09:01:33 the first built page was visible: a new homepage http://info.cern.ch - home of the first website with the button Browse the first website, two generated images (an early-90s workstation and an accelerator tunnel), and the pages /who-invented-the-world-wide-web and /404, 3 pages in all. Ploy said I made your new homepage. It's publishing now; once it's live I'll share the links., and at 09:03 Publish finished on a production and a staging address on a Ploy subdomain. Time: about 6 minutes from entering the site to the first built page and about 8 minutes to published, with 11 clicks and 3 answers. Approval: there was no separate plan or quote of what a rebuild would cost and no list of pages to approve; the agent built the pages straight after the three choice questions and published them to the Ploy subdomain without asking. The real site info.cern.ch was not touched and no own domain was connected. Credits: Settings, Usage showed AI credits 89 / 700 (Resets Nov 20) and Lifetime credits 89 / 2,000 straight after the onboarding, then 395 / 700 and 417 / 700 after the homepage (Today 421). By chat: Getting Started 226 (design system, two images, homepage and one more page), SEO & AEO audit 194 (started by itself in the onboarding) and other activity 1. Building one page with its design system cost about 226 credits, about a third of the daily 700. Contact credits 0 / 25. Plans: In the app (Settings, Billing): Free, 700 AI credits a day, 700 credits / day (2,000 max), without custom domains or enriched traffic data. Starter $50, now $40 per month, billed annually (Save $120 per year), 4,000 credits / month, 1 custom domain, Google Ads, Meta Ads and LinkedIn Ads, 25 contact lookup credits, 50 visitor enrichment credits and CRM integrations, with A/B testing marked coming soon. Pro $300, now $240 per month, billed annually (Save $720 per year), 24,000 credits / month, 5 custom domains, 150 contact lookup credits and 1,000 visitor enrichment credits. Extra AI credits can be bought, and 100 contact credits cost $25. On the public pricing page ploy.ai/pricing: Free $0, No credit card required, 500 credits / day (2,000 max); Starter $50/mo, 4,000 credits / month, 1 custom domain; Pro $300/mo, 24,000 credits / month, 5 custom domains, CRM integrations (HubSpot, Attio); Enterprise Custom. Billed annually, Starter is $480 a year ($40 a month) and Pro $2,880 a year ($240 a month). The free allowance differs: the pricing page says 500 credits a day, the app says 700 credits a day, both with a 2,000 maximum. Checkout: Billing, Starter, Upgrade opened Stripe Checkout at once for a Starter subscription, billed annually, EUR 454.53, with fields for card number, expiry and security code, Apple Pay and Link. Nothing was filled in and the page was left at once. The Stripe page was in Dutch, so no image of it was kept. A card was not asked at sign-up, onboarding, building or publishing to the Ploy subdomain, only at the upgrade. Cancelling: on the Free plan there is nothing to cancel and Billing shows only Upgrade; cancelling or changing a paid plan was not seen. Settings, Personal has a profile and no delete button that we saw; Security has password, passkey and Log out. Workspace General has a Danger Zone with Delete Workspace, which was not clicked. Not tested: the HubSpot and Attio links (Pro), connecting an own domain (Starter), Slack, Google Analytics and Search Console, publishing to an own domain, the full result of the SEO & AEO audit, A/B testing (coming soon), entering a card and cancelling a paid plan. Clean up: the account and the workspace with the info.cern.ch test project stay, and so do the two published Ploy subdomain pages, which are public and hold a redesign of info.cern.ch. The own tab was closed and our other tab was not touched. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Ploy starts two chats by itself in the onboarding and they spend credits in the background: the SEO & AEO audit used 194 credits before we asked for anything. There was no plan or price of the rebuild to approve; after three design questions the agent built the pages and published them on a public Ploy subdomain without asking. The free allowance is 700 credits a day in the app and 500 on the pricing page. The Stripe checkout followed the browser language rather than the English interface.
